acceptance.criterion_verbatim: is the chosen shape honest about its latency and its failure modes -- would an analyst who typed a ticker while the terminal was signed out see a MARKED failure with a reason, or a page that looks like it is still fetching an hour later?
acceptance.invocation: org/missions/D5/AMGT/AMGT_RESAPP/deliverables/0.9.0_WK_AMGT_RESAPP~2/SEAM_DESIGN.md sections 5 and 6, read against integrations/bloomberg/research/pull_consumer.py's process_one() and integrations/bloomberg/READ_HERE.md's sign-out rule; no single command decides it
acceptance.expect: a reading, recorded with no verdict
acceptance.output_evidence: SEAM_DESIGN.md section 5 states, and pull_consumer.py's process_one() implements: bloomberg_health() is called BEFORE every pull; on ok:False, packs/<security_key>/status.json is written {state: FAILED, reason: 'terminal signed out (bloomberg_health ok=False): <health error>'} and the SQS message is deleted -- no automatic retry, no sign-in attempt by this worker or this consumer. So an analyst who submits a ticker while the terminal is signed out would, once a consumer next drains the queue, see status.json move REQUESTED -> FAILED with a human-readable reason naming the health error -- a MARKED failure, not a page that looks like it is still fetching. The one honesty gap this design does NOT close: if NO consumer is running at all (the poller is a person-started/stopped process, or a daily-vehicle-invoked one-shot, per section 2 -- never a persistent service), a request sits at REQUESTED indefinitely with no FAILED/timeout state ever written, and status.json alone cannot distinguish 'about to be picked up' from 'no consumer will ever run.' SEAM_DESIGN.md section 6 states the measured latency (7.6s / 7.7s end to end for a cold request with the consumer launched in the same second) and is explicit that this number assumes a consumer is running; it does not assume an unbounded wait is honest UI behavior, but it also does not build a queue-age alarm (G-20 forbids one) or a status TIMEOUT state for an unattended queue -- left as a named gap for whichever cell next operationalizes the poller's own schedule.
